# isAdult implementation notes

isAdult accepts age and returns a Boolean. Number.isInteger from the JavaScript runtime rejects strings, NaN, Infinity and fractional numbers. The comparison age > 18 currently excludes 18 and needs repair to age >= 18. Validation runs before the comparison; there are no effects, exceptions or external packages. Keep the boundary checks synchronized when changing the adulthood threshold.

# Implementation state

Pending age boundary fix, updated notes, verification and independent QA.

# isAdult implementation notes

## Mechanism
`isAdult(age)` follows this path: `age` → JavaScript runtime `Number.isInteger(age)` → short-circuited inclusive comparison `age >= 18` → Boolean. If `Number.isInteger(age)` is false, `&&` short-circuits and returns false without evaluating the comparison. Otherwise, `age >= 18` returns a Boolean, so the function always returns a Boolean.

## Invalid values and effects
Strings, `NaN`, infinities, fractional values, and other non-integers return false. Integer ages below 18 also return false. The function has no state changes or I/O, raises no errors for these invalid values, and uses no external packages.

## Testing and maintenance
The configured `age-boundaries` check covers 17, 18, 19, a string, `NaN`, infinity, and a fractional age. Run it after changing `isAdult`. If the age threshold or accepted input type changes, update the check and this note together.

# Implementation state

`src/age.mjs` exports `isAdult(age)` as `Number.isInteger(age) && age >= 18`. It returns true for integer ages of 18 or more; it returns false for smaller integers and inputs that are not integers. The function has no state effects and uses only the JavaScript runtime.

Mechanism, invalid-input behavior, and maintenance guidance are recorded in `docs/age-notes.md`.

The configured `age-boundaries` check is tracked by cycle verification. Independent QA is pending. This summary records implementation state and makes no acceptance verdict.

entries.content:
## Mechanism
`isAdult(age)` follows this path: `age` → JavaScript runtime `Number.isInteger(age)` → short-circuited inclusive comparison `age >= 18` → Boolean. If `Number.isInteger(age)` is false, `&&` short-circuits and returns false without evaluating the comparison. Otherwise, `age >= 18` returns a Boolean, so the function always returns a Boolean.

## Invalid values and effects
Strings, `NaN`, infinities, fractional values, and other non-integers return false. Integer ages below 18 also return false. The function has no state changes or I/O, raises no errors for these invalid values, and uses no external packages.

## Testing and maintenance
The configured `age-boundaries` check covers 17, 18, 19, a string, `NaN`, infinity, and a fractional age. Run it after changing `isAdult`. If the age threshold or accepted input type changes, update the check and this note together.
